answerable_part: The file can show annual motorist deaths per police-reported crash, but has no miles-driven exposure and therefore cannot establish risk per mile or whether that risk declined.
metric: Motorists killed per 1,000 police-reported crashes in each calendar year.
denominator: Number of police-reported crashes with a usable motorist-death count in that calendar year; multiply deaths per crash by 1,000.
population: Police-reported NYC crashes with a usable crash_date in 2013-2025 and a nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed value.
years: Calendar years 2013-2025 inclusive; 2025 will be checked for partial coverage.

data_check.facts: check_2.csv reports 2,132,218 dated crashes in 2013-2025 and zero null crash dates; each year has records dated Jan 1 through Dec 31, including 85,546 crashes in 2025; no 1900-01-01 or 1970-01-01 date placeholders were found. number_of_motorist_killed is INT, and no values are missing in any year.
data_check.meaning_and_decisions: No selected crash rows need to be dropped for missing dates or motorist-death counts; thus all dated crashes contribute to the denominator. Keep the complete selected population. The full-year date endpoints show no year that is partial by recorded date range; this does not establish completeness of reporting or provide mileage exposure. Typed DATE and INT columns preclude empty-string or word-valued unknowns.

limitations: This is motorist deaths per police-reported crash, not risk per mile: vehicle-miles traveled are absent, and a crash-based denominator is not a measure of driving exposure. It describes recorded crash dates; the date span does not verify reporting completeness.
